title: Criminal conspiracy - why it remains one of the hardest charges to prove
p1: A group of people can commit a serious crime together, yet proving their hidden agreement can be the biggest challenge. Criminal conspiracy is often easier to allege than to establish.
p2: Many assume that being connected to a crime is enough for a conspiracy charge. The surprising part: the law usually requires proof of an agreement between people to commit an illegal act, not just suspicion, association, or similar actions.
p3: The difficulty lies in finding evidence of an invisible decision. Unlike a physical act caught on camera, a conspiracy often happens through private conversations, coded messages, or indirect arrangements. Investigators must connect the dots and show that the accused shared a common plan. The practical takeaway: strong evidence of intent and agreement matters more than mere presence around an offence.
conclusion: Do you think proving a hidden agreement should require more evidence than proving a direct criminal act?
